title: Fine-grain burst mitigation for trace hotpath with minimal allocs
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Why: We observe that under short, high-QPS bursts the tracing hotpath contributes disproportionate CPU variance and tail latency spikes (allocations and mutex contention during sample decision + enrichment). This is visible on console latency dashboards and correlates with increased p99 response times for inference pods during traffic spikes. Goal: reduce per-request tracing CPU overhead during bursts by >4x (target: <0.3% CPU overhead at 2k RPS burst) while preserving tail-capture fidelity for posthoc analysis.

What we will build: a lightweight two-stage trace probe that makes a micro-decision in the hotpath using a single atomic + bloom-prefilter, defers expensive context enrichment to an async writer, and uses a bounded per-thread ring buffer with backpressure signals. Key components: (1) fast-path probe skeletonization: write a 32B provenance token and tiny header into the request context with zero allocations on the hotpath; (2) ingress bloom prefilter that cheaply rejects low-tail-probability requests before sampler evaluation; (3) burst-aware micro-reservoir that reserves slots for enriching N traces per-second with age-based replenishment; (4) deferred enrichment worker that attaches full span metadata off-hotpath and emits to span sink; (5) graceful fallback: when ring buffer is full, emit only provenance token for later reconstruction.

Design constraints and non-goals: must avoid global locks and per-request heap allocations. We will not change sampling policy semantics (retain semantic guarantees for long-lived tails) and will not modify customer-visible trace IDs. This ticket focuses on engineering the low-allocation hotpath primitives and integration tests; telemetry/console visualization adjustments are covered in follow-ups.

Trade-offs: slightly increased complexity in reconstructing full trace context for very short-lived bursts, but this is mitigated by provenance token rehydration and a short retention window in the enrichment queue. The approach biases for minimal runtime cost over perfect inlining of every metadata field.
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath probe performs sampling decision and emits provenance token with zero heap allocations in >95% of requests (verified via pprof)
End-to-end p95 request latency regression <= 50us in microbench with instrumentation enabled
CPU overhead at a 2k RPS burst reduced to <0.3% (baseline ~1.8%) across representative inference service instances
Deferred enrichment successfully rehydrates >= 99.5% of captured provenance tokens within 10s under normal load
Automated integration test that simulates burst traffic passing with no global mutex contention

2025-02-25 - Devon Martinez: Implemented probe skeleton and bloom prefilter prototype. Microbench shows allocation drop from 48B/request to 0B for fast-path. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/11842
